name: LaunchDarkly
description: Protects against destructive LaunchDarkly CLI and API operations.

destructive_patterns.name: ldcli-flags-delete
destructive_patterns.description: ldcli flags delete permanently removes a feature flag. This cannot be undone.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a LaunchDarkly flag permanently removes it from all environments. \ SDKs will return default values, potentially breaking feature gates. Targeting \ rules, prerequisites, and experiment data are lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - ldcli flags archive: Soft-delete with recovery option \ - Turn off the flag in all environments first \ - Export flag configuration before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: ldcli-flags-archive
destructive_patterns.description: ldcli flags archive soft-deletes a feature flag. While recoverable, this affects all environments.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Archiving a flag removes it from the flag list and evaluation. While archived \ flags can be restored, SDKs will stop receiving the flag and return defaults \ immediately across all environments.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Turn off the flag before archiving \ - Verify no code paths depend on the flag \ - Document the flag's purpose before archiving

destructive_patterns.name: ldcli-projects-delete
destructive_patterns.description: ldcli projects delete removes an entire project and all its flags, environments, and settings.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a project removes ALL flags, environments, segments, and metrics \ within it. This is irreversible and affects all applications using this \ project's SDK keys.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Export project configuration first \ - Archive flags individually to preserve recovery options \ - Migrate critical flags to another project

destructive_patterns.name: ldcli-environments-delete
destructive_patterns.description: ldcli environments delete removes an environment and all its flag configurations.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an environment removes all flag configurations, targeting rules, \ and SDK keys for that environment. Applications using this environment's \ SDK key will fail to connect.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Rotate SDK keys before deletion \ - Export environment configuration \ - Turn off all flags in the environment first

destructive_patterns.name: ldcli-segments-delete
destructive_patterns.description: ldcli segments delete removes a user segment and its targeting rules.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a segment removes user grouping rules across all environments. \ Flags targeting this segment will lose that targeting, changing which \ users receive which variations.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review which flags use this segment \ - Update flag targeting before deletion \ - Export segment configuration

destructive_patterns.name: ldcli-metrics-delete
destructive_patterns.description: ldcli metrics delete removes a metric and its experiment data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a metric removes the metric definition and all associated \ experiment results. Historical experiment data for this metric is lost \ and cannot be recovered.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Export experiment results first \ - Archive the metric if possible \ - Document metric findings before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: launchdarkly-api-delete-environments
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to LaunchDarkly API removes environments.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
API DELETE calls to environments immediately invalidate SDK keys and remove \ all flag configurations for that environment. Connected applications will \ lose flag evaluations.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use ldcli for better confirmation prompts \ - GET the environment config first \ - Rotate SDK keys before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: launchdarkly-api-delete-flags
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to LaunchDarkly API removes feature flags.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
API DELETE calls permanently remove flags without archive recovery options. \ All targeting rules, variations, and prerequisites are lost across all \ environments.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use ldcli flags archive for soft-delete \ - GET the flag configuration first \ - Use the LaunchDarkly UI for visibility

destructive_patterns.name: launchdarkly-api-delete-segments
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to LaunchDarkly API removes segments.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
API DELETE calls to segments remove user groupings immediately. Flags \ using this segment will lose targeting rules, changing feature behavior \ for those users.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Check segment dependencies first \ - Update flag targeting before deletion \ - Export segment membership

destructive_patterns.name: launchdarkly-api-delete-projects
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to LaunchDarkly API removes projects.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
API DELETE calls to projects remove ALL resources: flags, environments, \ segments, metrics, and SDK keys. This is the most destructive operation \ and cannot be undone.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Export project configuration completely \ - Use ldcli for confirmation prompts \ - Contact LaunchDarkly support for assistance

destructive_patterns.name: launchdarkly-api-delete-generic
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to LaunchDarkly API can remove resources.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Generic DELETE requests to the LaunchDarkly API can remove various \ resources including webhooks, integrations, teams, and access tokens. \ Review the specific endpoint before executing.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Verify the exact resource being deleted \ - Use the LaunchDarkly UI for better visibility \ - GET the resource first to confirm
